articles.title: Automated Testing ROI: A Developer's Guide to QA That Pays
articles.excerpt: Developers know the feeling: a release goes out, a test you meant to write catches nothing because it was never written, and a bug that a ten-line check would have caught becomes a hotfix. This post i…
articles.body: Developers know the feeling: a release goes out, a test you meant to write catches nothing because it was never written, and a bug that a ten-line check would have caught becomes a hotfix. This post is the founder-facing case for automated testing, translated into developer terms: which checks pay for themselves, which ones rot, and how a small regression pack changes release day. Here is the direct answer. Automated testing saves budgets when it catches the same expensive mistakes early, every time, without paying a person to repeat the same checks by hand. It does not make a website bug free. It makes the cost of finding bugs predictable, and it stops small regressions from turning into emergency fixes.

articles.title: AI Automation Threatens Technical Jobs: Balancing Innovation with Workforce Security and Ethical Funding.
articles.excerpt: Introduction: The AI Revolution and Its Impact The AI revolution is here, and it’s not just knocking on the door—it’s kicking it down. Every day, we hear about breakthroughs in machine learning, natur…
articles.body: Introduction: The AI Revolution and Its Impact The AI revolution is here, and it’s not just knocking on the door—it’s kicking it down. Every day, we hear about breakthroughs in machine learning , natural language processing , and automation that promise to reshape industries. But beneath the glossy headlines lies a simmering tension: as AI gets better at automating tasks, it threatens to devalue the very specialized technical knowledge that built these systems in the first place. This isn’t just about machines replacing jobs—it’s about the erosion of expertise, the misallocation of resources, and the growing disconnect between hype and reality. Take, for example, the server management process.

articles.title: Building passkey-based verification without trusting the browser.
articles.excerpt: Most applications need to answer a deceptively simple question: should this request be allowed to continue? Historically, many applications have relied on CAPTCHAs, SMS one-time passwords, or custom b…
articles.body: Most applications need to answer a deceptively simple question: should this request be allowed to continue? Historically, many applications have relied on CAPTCHAs, SMS one-time passwords, or custom browser-side checks. Each approach comes with trade-offs involving user friction, delivery costs, phishing risk, or the difficulty of determining what a client can actually prove. We have been building Chirograph Verify around a different approach: WebAuthn-based device verification, with the verification decision made on the server. We're launching Chirograph Verify on October 30, 2026, and I wanted to share the engineering ideas behind it.

articles.body: A visitor gives your repository a few seconds to decide whether it is worth reading, and a short explainer video can show what the project does faster than three paragraphs of README. GitHub plays MP4 files inside Markdown, so the video can sit at the top of the README. Write the script first One minute of narration at a normal speaking pace is about 150 words. Use this shape: 1. The problem, in one sentence a user would say. (~20 words) 2. Who it is for. (~15 words) 3. What the project does, as three short beats. (~50 words) 4. One concrete example with real input and output. (~45 words) 5. How to get started: the install command or the link. articles.title: Keyboard focus: the five checks that catch most accessibility bugs in a form
articles.excerpt: Most keyboard problems in forms are visible in two minutes with nothing but the Tab key. Unplug the mouse and walk through the page. Can you see where you are? Every interactive element needs a visibl…
articles.body: Most keyboard problems in forms are visible in two minutes with nothing but the Tab key. Unplug the mouse and walk through the page. What to check Can you see where you are? Every interactive element needs a visible focus indicator. outline: none without a replacement fails WCAG 2.4.7 (Focus Visible). Prefer :focus-visible so mouse clicks stay quiet while keyboard users get a clear ring. Does the order match the reading order? Tab follows DOM order. If CSS reorders things visually (flex order , grid placement, absolute positioning), keyboard order and visual order drift apart (WCAG 2.4.3). Can you get out? A modal must move focus in on open, keep it inside, close on Escape, and return focus to the button that opened it. A focus trap with no exit is a hard blocker.

articles.title: oxipng after pngquant: about a second per three PNGs, big win on photos, a shrug on illustrations
articles.excerpt: Before deciding whether to keep oxipng behind pngquant, I wanted to know what that second step buys in bytes and in seconds. The check below used 12 PNGs from Wikimedia Commons (CC licenses), three ea…
articles.body: Before deciding whether to keep oxipng behind pngquant, I wanted to know what that second step buys in bytes and in seconds. The check below used 12 PNGs from Wikimedia Commons (CC licenses), three each of screenshots, icons, illustrations and photos, on an Apple M4 with pngquant 3.0.3 and oxipng 10.2.1. Sizes are exact bytes (oxipng prints KiB next to them, but I only quote bytes), and I did not compare image quality at all. What the second step looks like on one file Start with the first icon in the set, 40,369 bytes. pngquant at quality 65–80 got it to 7,600 and exited with 0. The extra step is one command, oxipng -o 4 --strip safe on a copy of the pngquant output, and it took the file to 6,954.

articles.body: Most SEO advice is written for SaaS companies and blogs. But what happens when you’re helping a traditional brand, in my case a dairy with 25+ years of offline trust, compete online for a keyword like “pure cow ghee”? Here are the lessons I learned from optimizing a Shopify store in one of the most crowded food categories in India. Lesson 1: The keyword is crowded, so be specific “Pure cow ghee” is a high-competition term. Big marketplaces and national brands dominate it. Instead of fighting head-on, I built content around the questions buyers actually ask: How to check if ghee is pure Cow ghee vs buffalo ghee Is A2 ghee worth the price Best ghee for pongal and South Indian sweets These pages bring smaller but much more qualified traffic.

articles.body: TL;DR Google Photos has fixed a bug that made edited pictures disappear from other Android apps. The issue affected photo pickers and apps like Google Messages, Gemini, and WhatsApp. The fix is available in Google Photos v7.97. Your perfectly edited photo is ready for its grand WhatsApp debut. You open the app, tap the image picker, and suddenly your masterpiece pulls a disappearing act. No warning, no error message. Just an empty spot where your picture should be. For some Google Photos users, this wasn’t a magic trick. It was an irritating bug that turned a routine photo edit into a game of hide-and-seek across Android apps. Thankfully, Google appears to have finally called time on the disappearing act.

articles.body: Full spoilers follow for Avatar: Seven Havens Season 1, Episodes 10-13! articles.excerpt: Review: Nocturne Episodes 1 & 2 are threading a needle as it hopes to intrigue viewers with familiar tropes delivered in a remixed storyline.
articles.body: Spoilers follow for Nocturne Episodes 1 and 2, which are available on Apple TV now. Apple TV’s new thriller series, Nocturne, aims to draw audiences in with just the right balance of the familiar and the unexpected. The show asks what happens when a boy thought to be the victim of a serial killer returns alive, and follows the criminal mastermind as he maneuvers law enforcement during their race to save any other victims who may still be out there. Over the course of these first two episodes, viewers are left with questions — a mix of plot-driven intrigue, interest in character development, and a touch of side-eye around potential logic gaps or plot conveniences. Nocturne is based on Lars Kepler’s crime novels (The Sandman and Lazarus), and adapted by Rowan Joffe and John Hlavin for TV.

articles.title: Halloween Aboard the International Space Station
articles.excerpt: Although no ghouls, goblins, or trick-or-treaters come knocking at the International Space Station’s front hatch, crew members aboard the orbiting laboratory still like to get in the Halloween spirit.…
articles.body: ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano finally gets his wish to fly like Superman aboard the International Space Station during Expedition 37. Although no ghouls, goblins, or trick-or-treaters come knocking at the International Space Station’s front hatch, crew members aboard the orbiting laboratory still like to get in the Halloween spirit. Whether individually or as an entire crew, they dress up in sometimes spooky, sometimes scary, but always creative costumes, often designed from materials available aboard the space station.   Take a look at how the station crews have celebrated in years past. For Halloween 2009, the Expedition 21 crew shows off its costumes. Expedition 21 NASA astronaut Nicole Stott shows off her Halloween costume.

articles.title: You can generate and edit Google Docs files directly in Gemini chats now
articles.excerpt: Now you can generate, preview, and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code directly within Google Gemini. The new file editing capabilities are availabl…
articles.body: Now you can generate, preview, and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code directly within Google Gemini . The new file editing capabilities are available starting today for all Gemini users, and while PDF previews/editing works on both the web and mobile, all other file formats are only in the web version for now. Google added support for generating and downloading files in Gemini earlier this year, but now you can tweak those files without leaving the Gemini app. Google says you can expand documents to edit them in full-screen mode and highlight text in files to ask Gemini questions or prompt … Read the full story at The Verge.
